# Instructions

This week, you worked with three new data types in R -- factors, strings, and date-times -- using the forcats, stringr, and lubridate packages, respectively.

In this milestone, you'll plot the CAGRs for each index and sector we've examined, in a single plot ordered from largest CAGR to smallest.

To learn more about the variables contained in the data sets, refer to the data dictionaries for `indexes` (https://rstudio.github.io/academy-tidyverse-stock-portfolios/assets/indexes_dictionary.html), `sp500` (https://rstudio.github.io/academy-tidyverse-stock-portfolios/assets/sp500_dictionary.html), and `sectors` (https://rstudio.github.io/academy-tidyverse-stock-portfolios/assets/sectors_dictionary.html).

Remember that all tidyverse packages have already been installed for you but you will need to *load* the ones you want to use.

### Part 2 - Prepare the data

Run the code below to recreate the variables we have made in previous milestones. This produces `index_cagrs` (the CAGR for each index) and `sector_cagrs` (the CAGR for each sector).

```{r}
#| label: prep-data
#| message: false
index_cagrs <-
  indexes |>
  mutate(
    symbol = case_when(
      symbol == "^DJI"  ~ "Dow Jones",
      symbol == "^FVX"  ~ "5 Year Treasury",
      symbol == "^GSPC" ~ "S&P 500",
      symbol == "^IRX"  ~ "13 Week Treasury",
      symbol == "^IXIC" ~ "NASDAQ",
      symbol == "^TNX"  ~ "10 Year Treasury"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(symbol) |>
  summarise(CAGR = ((last(adjusted) / first(adjusted)) - 1) * 100) |>
  ungroup()

sp500_tidy <-
  sp500 |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = event, values_from = price)

sector_prices <-
  sp500_tidy |>
  left_join(sectors, by = "symbol") |>
  group_by(sector, date) |>
  summarise(daily_total = sum(adjusted, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup()

sector_cagrs <-
  sector_prices |>
  group_by(sector) |>
  summarise(CAGR = ((last(daily_total) / first(daily_total)) - 1) * 100)

sector_cagrs
```

## Part 4 - The role of factor orders in visualizations

Run the chunk below to visualize the data of `cagrs`.

```{r}
#| label: summary-plot
#| eval: false
cagrs |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(y = symbol, x = CAGR)) +
  geom_col()
```

This is a nice plot, but the order of symbols on the y axis is arbitrary (alphabetical). We may want to give the symbols a more principled order before we publish this plot.

Using the code chunk below, investigate a research question about this data, using the skills you have learned this week and in previous weeks of Academy. Some ideas:

1. Use data visualization to investigate if there seems to be a trend in stock value (variable of your choosing) _within the year_ -- for all indices, certain sectors, or focal companies within a sector.
2. Is there a _quarterly_ pattern for stock returns? Does this change if you focus on certain indices, sectors, or companies within a sector?
3. Looking _within_ a month, do you see patterns in returns, open/close price, high/low value, or volume? Do these patterns map to day of the week? If you look across months, do patterns emerge by day of the month?
